provider: Koyeb (Paris, France; acquired by Mistral AI, announced 2026-02-17) - Serverless GPU, 1x NVIDIA L4 24GB instance, scale-to-zero
region_dc: Koyeb core regions: Frankfurt (fra), Paris (par), Washington D.C., Singapore, Tokyo. L4 GPU availability in Paris/Frankfurt specifically is [uncertain] (not confirmed from the regions/instances docs, which could not be fetched; Frankfurt is the historically documented GPU EU region). Post-acquisition EU region status [uncertain]: Koyeb said the platform continues operating and will become a core component of Mistral Compute; no announced removal of EU regions found.
sovereignty_class: EU HQ (Paris, FR) and EU DC, now owned by Mistral AI (French, EU HQ) - full EU sovereignty profile on paper; no US parent so no direct CLOUD Act exposure at the corporate level [uncertain: upstream bare-metal/DC provider not verified]. Certifications: SOC 2 attested (per GetDeploying); no SecNumCloud, BSI C5, HDS or ISO 27001 found [uncertain]. Mistral positions Koyeb as part of 'sovereign AI infrastructure in Europe'.
monthly_cost: List price USD 0.70/h (~EUR 0.62/h) for 1x L4, 1-second billing. 24/7 = ~USD 511/mo (~EUR 450/mo), 3x over the EUR 150 budget, so 24/7 always-on is not viable. POC-hours: 50 h/mo ~ USD 35 (~EUR 31); 100 h/mo ~ USD 70 (~EUR 62); ~240 active h/mo is the break-even for the EUR 150 cap. Plan fee (Pro/Scale) plus egress extra [uncertain: plan fee amount and whether new signups can get GPU access are unverified].
billing_granularity: Per-second; scale-to-zero supported on GPU (sleeping service is free, billed only while running). Agentic idle-heavy: idle periods cost nothing only if the service sleeps; sleep delay is configurable but each wake costs a cold start, and a continuously chatty agent session that keeps the instance awake pays full rate.
setup_fee_and_lockin: No setup fee. No commitment on on-demand; optional savings plans up to 50% off for long-term reservations. Exit cost: container-based, low (standard Docker image). Enterprise has a monthly minimum. Starter tier closed to new signups (TechCrunch 2026-02); GetDeploying notes restricted new signups since Sept 2026 [uncertain exactly what access a new account gets, may require Pro or sales contact].
gen_tps_7b_q4: [uncertain] Bandwidth-derived, not measured: L4 has ~300 GB/s, 4.4 GB Q4_K_M weights gives ~68 t/s theoretical ceiling, realistic ~40-55 t/s decode with llama.cpp CUDA.
prefill_tps: [uncertain] Bandwidth/compute-derived estimate, not measured: roughly 2000-3500 t/s prompt processing for 7B Q4_K_M on L4 with llama.cpp (CUDA, flash-attn).
ttft_at_4k: Warm instance: ~1.5-3 s at 4k prompt tokens (task-supplied figure, consistent with prefill estimate of ~1.2-2 s plus overhead) [uncertain: not measured]. Cold start from zero adds container pull plus model load of 4.5 GB; likely tens of seconds to a few minutes unless the model is baked into the image or on a volume [uncertain].
concurrency_slots: [uncertain] 24 GB VRAM minus 4.5 GB weights leaves ~18 GB for KV. For a Mistral-7B-class arch (GQA, 8 KV heads) KV is ~0.125 GB per 1k tokens at f16, so 4 slots (-np 4) at 16k ctx each is ~8 GB, 8 slots feasible. Single-GPU compute bounds throughput, not VRAM.
ctx_ram_headroom: L4 24 GB VRAM: after 4.5 GB model, ~18 GB for KV and compute buffers. Full 32k context (Bielik 7B v0.1 trained at 8k-32k depending on version [uncertain]) fits easily with several slots; the practical limit is model-native context, not memory. Instance RAM and disk sizes for the L4 type were not verified [uncertain].
availability_status: Available on demand for existing accounts; L4 listed at USD 0.70/h by multiple trackers (GetDeploying, cloudgpuprices). New-signup access is restricted since the Mistral acquisition (Starter closed; restricted new signups as of Sept 2026 per GetDeploying), so effectively gated / contact-sales for new customers [uncertain]. GPU stock is quota-gated and may require a request.
egress_traffic: 1 TB/month included on the plan; overage USD 0.02/GB (US and EU), USD 0.04/GB Asia (GetDeploying). Agentic LLM traffic is tiny, egress is a non-issue.
electricity_metering: Not applicable (cloud, not colo). For reference, an L4 draws ~72 W TDP; power is bundled in the hourly price.
hosting_model: Self-host: you deploy your own Docker image (llama.cpp server, Bielik GGUF Q4_K_M) as a Koyeb Service on a GPU instance. Full control of chat template, parser and flags (--jinja, tool-call grammar). Not a managed model API; model fetched from HF/volume at startup (use a Volume or baked image to cut cold start).
tool_calling_support: Depends entirely on the user's llama.cpp build: llama-server --jinja provides OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions with server-side tool-call parsing for supported templates. Bielik's template/parser compatibility is not Koyeb-specific and must be validated [uncertain].
spec_decode_support: Yes, in principle: self-hosted llama.cpp can load a draft model (-md) on the same GPU; 24 GB VRAM has ample room for the 7B target plus a small draft. Bielik DFlash draft compatibility with llama.cpp is not verified here [uncertain].
sla_uptime: SLA only on the Scale plan (per GetDeploying: Scale adds seats, AWS regions and an uptime SLA); exact percentage not verified [uncertain]. No SLA on Pro/Starter; scale-to-zero cold starts are not covered.
llm_inference_tos: LLM inference is the primary advertised use case (Koyeb AI / serverless GPU inference page, deploying models from Mistral and others). No restriction found.
price_stability: Mixed. Koyeb cut L4/L40S/A100 prices in Dec 2024. The L4 price is USD 0.70/h in current trackers. Post-acquisition risk is elevated: pivot to enterprise focus, Starter closed, platform to merge into Mistral Compute 'over the coming months' (Feb 2026), so pricing, plan structure and EU regions may change [uncertain]. Prices are quoted in USD, so EUR cost floats with FX.
model_lock_in: Low model lock-in: you bring your own GGUF container, so Bielik cannot be removed from a catalog. Platform lock-in risk is the acquisition: the product may be re-platformed or folded into Mistral Compute with migration needed, and access for new users is restricted.
